chunks.say: In nineteen seventy-seven, a telescope heard a signal from space for seventy-two seconds…
chunks.cap: In 1977, a telescope heard a signal from space for 72 seconds…

chunks.say: and never heard it again.
What if it came back?
Tonight, a radio telescope picks it up.
Same frequency. Same patch of sky.
And this time… it doesn't stop.
It's coming from a planet fourteen hundred light-years away.
This message was sent long before anyone on Earth had a telescope.
Within an hour, every phone on the planet is buzzing.
Scientists find a pattern.
Prime numbers.
Two, three, five, seven.
Nature doesn't count in primes. Someone made this.
Then the numbers become a picture.
A map. Fourteen pulsars… all pointing to one tiny star.
Ours.
But here's the problem.
Our first radio signals have only traveled about a hundred light-years.
They can't have heard us.
So how did they know we were here?
They didn't hear us. They saw our air.
Oxygen. The fingerprint of life… that Earth has been breathing out for two billion years.
We could answer. But a reply would take fourteen hundred years to get there.
So… would you reply?
